HILLBROW AFTER DARK

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Hillbrow after dark – we hit the grimy streets on night duty with a security company in Joburg’s inner city hub of crime.

Unique Selling Point:
** UNIQUE INSIGHT TO A WORLD FEW OF OUR VIEWERS HAVE ACCESS TO
** ACTION SCENES


Summary:
Once the cosmopolitan centre of Joburg, today the seedy underbelly of inner city crime and decay.

Carte Blanche spends a night on the streets with a local security guard seeing firsthand what goes down after dark in a part of the city that very few outsiders venture into after sunset.



Further information:
It’s a part of the city that has a rich history – but today is home to mostly foreigners struggling to make ends meet, this part of town is alive with people hustling and bustling. There are street hawkers, fast food joints and criminal operations – from drugs to fake ID producers to stolen technology dealers.

It’s a eat or be eaten kind of world. Pick pockets and cellphone snatchers feed off easy targets. Thugs hijack buildings, holding landlords and undocumented tenants to ransom. It’s dark world, that is filled with a fight to survive.

We join a guard from a local security company on a night shift in Hillbrow.

WHAT WE CAN EXPECT
This particular company monitors close to 200 buildings, their tenants and the wider community in Hillbrow. It gets messy on the streets - from petty theft to violent attacks, shops dealing in stolen goods and fronts for online cons and then of course there's the drugs and booze. This company has a network of cameras across Hillbrow, gives it a lekker big brother layer.

THE CHARACTER
The main character is a guy I've worked with before - Rashad Mahomed aka “Corky” - he speaks well - he's funny and fearless - can't help but chase down crooks - it's in his blood. We’ll arrange to start the shift at this home and get a sunset kind of vibe as he leaves his family and starts his shift.

PLAYING IT BY EAR
After the first night – we’ll decide what other elements we’ll need. AM suggested Nigel Branken – who is a social worker / academic living in Hillbrow – he might be a good “analyst” from the inside.

ADDITIONAL INTERVIEWS
** We’ll pick up vox pop style interviews as we go from scene to scene.

STRUCTURE: HILLBROW AFTER DARK.

VO: Hillbrow. Once the cosmopolitan playground of Joburg’s middle-class. Today, the seedy underbelly of an inner city lost to crime and decay.

On this month-end Friday, the streets feel chaotic.

LINK: We've just arrived at the headquarters of one of the biggest security companies in Hillbrow. They have a very tough job.

VO: Hendrik de Klerk is Hillbrow born and raised. He lives and breathes this neighbourhood.

DE KLERK: Back to the corner. // Where there was selling the drugs //.

VO: This team keeps a watchful eye over the area, using a network of CCTV cameras, guards, street patrollers and undercover agents.

DE KLERK: //IT’S not just crime. We look for human behaviour. //

VO : Situations can turn volatile in seconds. It’s impossible to predict, and no two shifts are ever the same.

DE KLERK: You know what? We don't expect the worst. If you expect the worst, you don't want to be here, You know, we want to be here. // Even though it's very, very dangerous.

VO: Tonight we’re going on a ride along in this eat or be eaten world. De Klerk is armed and clearly alert. But he seems oddly at ease as we navigate the streets.

MASA: Are you always armed?
DE KLERK: Nah, Just when I feel like it, I don't feel threatened in Hillbrow.
MASA: You one of the very few people. //DD1M5
INTERACTION WITH STREET PEOPLE… Papa D….
DE KLERK: How you? you alright? Just wait for me.
MASA: You’re Popular.
DE KLERK: People respect us. It doesn't matter who they are.

VO: Our first stop is one of the buildings managed by De Klerk’s crew. With 350 flats, about 2600 people call this home.

MASA: Let’s take a look…

VO: For a different perspective of Hillbrow, we’re heading up.

DE KLERK and you just climb up
MASA: Oh okay.

VO: All the way up.

MASA: It’s quite impressive from up here… but you know just the contrast looking how many building are in this side//
DE KLERK: /The noise, the sound, just close your eyes for a minute and just take it in

MOMENT….

DE KLERK: // People are using the top of the roofs now for safe zones – they don’t let the kids play in the street.
DE KLERK: //that building – that one there, it's been totally stripped.
MASA: yah
DE KLERK: Every window frame, whatever is a piece of steel is on a boat on the way to China. That's how bad that building is. Because there's no management, there's no owner and there's no one to look after that building.

MOMENT….

DE KLERK: //Hillbrow is not a bad place. We just need to fix it.

VO: The densely populated high rises are home to a mix of South Africans and foreigners – people looking for opportunities and trying to make ends meet.

DE KLERK: Hillbrow is hugely overcrowded. Some people, the same bed there's somebody sleeping in a day. Somebody sleeping in the night.
MASA: A lot of people say that Hillbrow is a nest for criminals to come and hide out here?
DE KLERK: I would agree with it. // a lot of our fraudsters, the city guys that, uh, courier robbers, they are from countries, cross border countries, and they live in this buildings because they're undetected.

LINK: As the sun sets here, the energy changes, the music gets louder and the dark side of Hillbrow comes out.

MONTAGE OF CCTV FOOTAGE – NIGHT ROBBERIES

VO: Taking to the streets here is like running a gauntlet - assaults, stabbings, and deadly shootings are horrifyingly frequent.

Recent Hillbrow crime stats show an increase in reported robbery, sexual assault and murder cases.

Crime victims are often resident here - but so are the perpetrators.

MASA: Is there ever even a peaceful night in Hillbrow?
DE KLERK: Not really. You can see how busy it is. you can see the hustle and the bustle//W2M2
DE KLERK: And this is where the crime comes //you have to be highly alert when you're around here, of the people on top of you, your personal space, you have to be alert.
MASA: There's a lot going on. W2M2
DE KLERK: And that's why it's important that the streetlights work, the urban management, all the lights are off this is the CBD. It needs to get on the.// The darker it is the more problems.// W2M3

VO: And it’s in these shadows that criminals lurk, taking cover after going on the hunt for easy targets.

Besides the many smaller dilapidated properties, there are at least six big abandoned buildings occupied illegally - usually paying rent to criminal syndicates.

DE KLERK: the guy with the biggest gun and the strongest arms for that timeframe runs the building.

DE KLERK: //It's quiet now because nobody wants to be outside now // It's a ruff, ruff, ruff area.there’s people living here
MASA: There’s people living, I can see. //
DE KLERK: They just hang some form of blankets
MASA: Oh wow - And how big of a problem are these hijacked buildings?
DE KLERK: A huge problem. // It's dropping the tenant rate of the building's next door. People are moving out faster
MASA: I must admit, if you weren't with us tonight, I would also be afraid to walk on the streets by myself.

VO : It’s a sentiment shared by residents of nearby blocks of flats.

VOX POP: //It brings crime, this building, so it's no longer safe to walk around, especially early in the morning and around evening ….

LINK: It really feels like Hillbrow has been left to rot. There's litter everywhere. Sewage in the streets. Abandoned buildings that have been hijacked…..

VO: Solutions will have to involve more than just security.

DE KLERK: We're not there just to fight crime. We're not just here to clean streets. We are to create a better neighborhood for everyone. We just need the political will, with the right investors, with the city,//Helping, evicting the problem buildings, helping cleaning up the infrastructure we can turn Hillbrow around.

VO: In the darkness, we come across a group of men huddled around a fire. Like many here - and perhaps ironically - they’re worried about crime..

MOMENT OF HELLO UP SOUNDS OVER WIDES MAYBE FIRE HOUSE

MASA: how bad is the crime here in hillbrow?
HOMELESSGUY: Is too too much. It's too. Much.
MASA Yeah.
HOMELESSGUY: Same street, on the other side a lot. This other building, the dirty one, a lot of things happening there.
DE KLERK: cAsa Mia - shootings, murder
HOMELESS GUY: Every day //

DE KLERK: These guys are our eyes and ears, they always come to me to come to the office and they say something is happening up and we're grateful.

VO: Largely unnoticed, De Klerk has an established network of sources across the neighbourhood.

PEOPLE CALLING DE KLERK – papa D –
DE KLERK: This connection is very, very important, Without them, we will be blind and we will not know what's going on

VO: De Klerk believes some of Hillbrow’s challenges are connected to an influx of undocumented foreign nationals.

DE KLERK: My point is we're not going to fix Hillbrow if we don't fix the rules for everyone. // I must have a permit for my house, for my borehole. I have a permit for my dogs. We are overregulated and people in Hillbrow just do what they want

VO: Illegal street drinking is the norm: here people drink, gamble and party on one street corner to the next.

DE KLERK: // the cooler brigades and it's the guys causing the problems // And at the end of the night they’re the victims, they're the ones getting robbed because they're so drunk.

VO: In this CCTV clip. a visibly drunk man is assaulted by criminals. When he tries to fight back, one of the assailants takes out a knife and brutally stabs him.

While these scenes are all too common on the streets of Hillbrow, as we discovered less violent drunken disputes are an almost daily occurrence.

2 SECONDS - UPSOUND MUSI SCUFFLE

VO: In response, registered taverns are doing what they can to keep their patrons off the streets - offering a safe venue with additional lighting and guards at the door checking for weapons.

DE KLERK: let me show you to what’s the nightlife in Hillbrow. Let's walk through. TD2M1

WALK THROUGH MOMENT

VO: While loud, from what we saw, these were just people out for a good time in a secure environment….

There’s been a drop in street prostitution in Hillbrow - but public drug abuse is getting out out of hand.

It costs these Nyope addicts R25 for a hit of the cheap heroin mix.

MASA: And how does it make you feel when you've had it?
DRUGGIE: too high
MASA: just stop
DRUGGIE: You can't survive a day without smoking.
MASA: So you need it
DRUGGIE: It’s like our medicine DR2M1

VO : They mix the Nyope with water and inject it into a vein using a mirror.

MASA: but there's a needle in your neck, is it not? So it's not painful for you.
DRUGGIE: Shakes head no….DR2M5

MASA: And you don't mind that you're doing it here in the street in the public. You don't. You're not scared. Maybe police will come.
DRUGGIE: No, no, we are scared, as you see, we hide.
MASA: you know that this is not a good thing.
DRUGGIE: /. You can't get by the counter – it’s illegal - you see? So that's why we say when we see the cops, we hide. You see, we hide.

VO: It’s been a relatively uneventful night. But with his shift now over, De Klerk acknowledges life in Hillbrow can be overwhelming.

DE KLERK: We don't work in Sandton, we don't work in malls, we work in the streets of Hillbrow. I'll see if I see death, I see poverty, I see drugs, and you have to switch off. // I believe in good. i can’t always beats evil. // I just want to make a small difference. Sometimes a bit tougher, but it's what we do. We go and make a difference in hillbrow.

metadata.Summary: Once the cosmopolitan centre of Joburg, today the seedy underbelly of inner city crime and decay. Carte Blanche spends a night on the streets with a local security guard seeing firsthand what goes down after dark in a part of the city that very few outsiders venture into after sunset.
metadata.Further information: It’s a part of the city that has a rich history – but today is home to mostly foreigners struggling to make ends meet, this part of town is alive with people hustling and bustling. There are street hawkers, fast food joints and criminal operations – from drugs to fake ID producers to stolen technology dealers. It’s a eat or be eaten kind of world. Pick pockets and cellphone snatchers feed off easy targets. Thugs hijack buildings, holding landlords and undocumented tenants to ransom. It’s dark world, that is filled with a fight to survive. We join a guard from a local security company on a night shift in Hillbrow. WHAT WE CAN EXPECT This particular company monitors close to 200 buildings, their tenants and the wider community in Hillbrow. It gets messy on the streets - from petty theft to violent attacks, shops dealing in stolen goods and fronts for online cons and then of course there's the drugs and booze. This company has a network of cameras across Hillbrow, gives it a lekker big brother layer. THE CHARACTER The main character is a guy I've worked with before - Rashad Mahomed aka “Corky” - he speaks well - he's funny and fearless - can't help but chase down crooks - it's in his blood. We’ll arrange to start the shift at this home and get a sunset kind of vibe as he leaves his family and starts his shift. PLAYING IT BY EAR After the first night – we’ll decide what other elements we’ll need. AM suggested Nigel Branken – who is a social worker / academic living in Hillbrow – he might be a good “analyst” from the inside. ADDITIONAL INTERVIEWS ** We’ll pick up vox pop style interviews as we go from scene to scene.
